claim: Transformational creativity has been formalised as a meta-level change of the rules, representation or hypothesis space (Wiggins CSF; Santo et al.; Schapiro et al.), but all formalisations are theory with no agent experiment.
agent_test: none needed; use as vocabulary. Label each agent edit as rule drop (O4), representation (O6) or goal reframe (O8).

claim: Novelty is neither sufficient nor (in general) necessary for transformation; it is necessary only for set-driven learners.
agent_test: Log whether a novel answer changed the solution frame or only the wording; compare rates.

claim: Editing the most upstream constraint (an axiom) has the largest transformative potential in a dependency-graph model.
agent_test: In O4 pick the constraint with most dependents first; compare to a random constraint at equal tokens on constraint-relaxation tasks.
gap_note: Gap 6: theorem is true by counting dependents; validity of edited-space solutions untested.

claim: No benchmark measures transformational creativity directly. AGC-Bench, CreativeBench and the Franceschelli-Musolesi papers all say it is untested; OMEGA, T-UoT and Bhushan's level-4 rubric are indirect proxies.
agent_test: Build a small in-house rule-change set (items where the familiar tactic provably fails) and report the O4/O6/O8 arms there.
gap_note: Gap 8: Baba Is AI (2024) is a verifiable rule-edit benchmark, but combinational; TwistBench and Spark unchecked.

claim: Position papers argue LLMs cannot do transformational creativity (training distribution, RLHF narrowing); this is asserted, not tested, and partly predates reasoning models and scaffolds.
agent_test: Check whether a scaffold run passes items where plain sampling at k=N never does (pass@k gap).

claim: Frontier LLMs fail OMEGA transformative items (new tactic needed); base accuracy typically below 20 percent, and RL on the familiar tactic does not teach the new one (one setting +10 pp, matrix rank OOD fell 30 pp).
agent_test: Run O6 (change representation, e.g. symmetry substitution prompt) vs plain on the OMEGA transformative split at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap 3: OMEGA transformative items were never tried with prompts or representation hints on frontier models.

claim: RL with verifiable rewards narrows rather than widens the solution space: pass@1 on training set rose 26.1 to 42.5 while pass@256 fell; base model wins at large k.
agent_test: Compare pass@1 with pass@k of scaffold vs base; credit the scaffold only if pass@k rises.
gap_note: Gap 4: distillation from a stronger teacher widens pass@k; RL does not. No scaffold test exists.

claim: An explicit rule-transformation procedure (T-UoT) gives little reliable gain: best on 2 of 3 GPT-4o tasks on 10 generations, 6th of 7 on HypoArena with Qwen3-14B (win 17.3 percent vs E-UoT 32.7), ablation 54.2 percent, and highest token cost.
agent_test: Replicate on one hypothesis set with a code or held-out check instead of LLM judge; cost-match to CoT.
gap_note: Gap 1: plain prompt is last on Qwen3-14B and first on GLM-4-9B; no token-matched run.

claim: T-UoT has two bottlenecks: carrying consequences of a rule edit into the final answer (7 of 12 largest failures) and admitting poor rule edits (5 of 12). Forcing one derived mechanistic consequence lifted one frozen case from rank 7 to 2.5; a diagnostic on hand-picked cases, not a test.
agent_test: After an O4 or O8 edit, require an explicit derived consequence step checked by code; ablate it.

claim: Scaffolds that propose and check unconventional tool-use hypotheses before acting (EscapeAgent Foresight+Reflection) cut steps and hints without training, e.g. GPT-4o 593.9 to 452.0 steps.
agent_test: Add a hypothesis-check-before-act step in an agent task; measure steps at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap 9: Foresight+Reflection cut GPT-4o hints about 49 percent and steps about 36 percent on the design benchmark; no replication or token accounting.

claim: Agents become less novel every episode and refine rather than abandon a novel approach: 87.0 percent (80/92) refined; abandon 6.5 percent for low-impact episodes vs 16.4 percent otherwise; novelty change is uncorrelated with score change.
agent_test: Add an impasse trigger to reframe after a flat score; check abandon rate and score at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap 7: search policies converge to the same P-creativity; no impasse-trigger arm.

claim: LLM ideas are rated more novel than expert ideas before execution (4.84 vs 5.64, N=49 each), but lose 1.05 points of novelty after execution vs about 0 for human ideas; novelty does not guarantee value.
agent_test: Select ideas by execution outcome in code, not model judgement; compare with model-picked ideas.

claim: Idea overgeneration saturates: of 4000 seeds per topic only about 200 (5 percent) are non-duplicate, so more samples do not give new frames.
agent_test: Measure unique-frame count per token for sample-more vs O4/O6/O8 forced-diverse prompts.

claim: Many LLMs give near-identical open-ended answers (79 percent of cases above 0.8 mean similarity; 61.2 percent of min-p same-model pairs above 0.8); highly open prompts are not more varied (0.800 vs 0.837). A reanalysis disputes the headline example and finds prompting raises diversity.
agent_test: Test whether an explicit frame-change instruction raises frame diversity versus temperature at equal tokens, using a matched same-prompt null.
gap_note: Gap 5: reanalysis shows two-cluster example fails (80.5 percent one vehicle in 750) and a residual effect survives a stronger null (about 2-3 times).

claim: Alignment lowers diversity and creativity indices: RLHF lowers CREATIVITY INDEX by 30.1 percent on average; aligned Llama-2 clusters more than base.
agent_test: Only relevant when comparing base and instruct backbones; try base-model sampling for O4 branches.

claim: Cheap levers move novelty: telling models to be creative (dz +1.40) and mid-range temperature (0.5-0.75); reasoning mode adds little (dz +0.34) and nothing on combination tasks.
agent_test: Include a plain 'be creative' arm and a temperature arm as controls; a rule-change operator must beat both at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap 1: verbalized sampling beats temperature on the diversity-quality front; temperature is only weakly tied to novelty.

claim: Larger models improve correctness and combination but not exploration or novelty (convergence by scaling).
agent_test: Check whether operator gains shrink with a stronger backbone.

claim: LLMs explore open-ended discovery poorly: Little Alchemy 2 elements in 500 trials, humans 42, GPT-4o 35, DeepSeek-R1 85, o1 177; prompt hints gave no significant gain (p=0.304).
agent_test: Run the scaffold on a Little Alchemy-style task; count elements at equal trials.

claim: LLM tool-repurposing: GPT-4 solves 73.3 percent vs humans 79.3 percent on MacGyver; main error is wrong tool use (42.4 percent); reflection helped GPT-4 only.
agent_test: Test an O6 'other function of the object' step on MacGyver items.

claim: Search over the rule or design space of the agent itself (ADAS, Darwin Godel Machine) gives measured gains: ADAS +13.6 F1 on DROP; DGM SWE-bench 20.0 to 50.0 percent, lower without the archive.
agent_test: Not a single-agent operator; consider as an offline way to tune the schema, counted in setup cost (G7).

claim: Alternating exploration and transformation works in a toy domain (DeLeNoX): the transforming run keeps diversity by its own metric; no human rating.
agent_test: Analogue: learn features from solutions found so far and reroute search; test on a puzzle set.

claim: Transfer strategies for conceptual change in CNNs show no single winner; keeping first-layer filters helps classification.
agent_test: Not applicable to a prompt-only agent.

claim: Automated creativity tests (DAT, RAT) have unproven validity for LLM scientific ideation; only DRAT predicted it.
agent_test: Do not use DAT or RAT as an agent-quality gauge; use execution outcomes.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A strong LLM judge reaches Spearman 0.732 with human novelty ratings (human alpha 0.724); judge quality scales with size.
agent_test: Use a judge only for triage; confirm by running.

claim: LLM judges used to rank rule-change scaffolds are only moderately consistent: pairwise Spearman 0.587-0.616 across three judges, hard A/B flips 2.6-5.4 percent, human-vs-LLM creativity r=0.708 at method level but novelty r=0.224.
agent_test: Rank O4 variants with a code or constraint check; use LLM judges only as a secondary column.

claim: A code-checked rule-edit test bed exists (Baba Is AI: break or make rules, exact-match plans); 2024 models fail when rule operations must be composed in a new order. It is closer to combination than to Boden transformation.
agent_test: Run plain, best-of-N, verbalized sampling and an O4 scaffold at equal tokens on Baba Is AI composition splits.

claim: Prompt rewording (persona, anti-modal, unexpected-domain) raises embedding diversity over the plain prompt in all 12 topics for most phrasings (25 of 30 tests at the p floor, 15 models); quality not measured.
agent_test: Compare an anti-modal reframe instruction with temperature at matched quality using a checker.

claim: Different agent search policies (greedy, MCTS, evolutionary) converge to similar low novelty within a few episodes, and change in novelty is uncorrelated with change in score (r between -0.111 and 0.056), so the scaffold around search dominates policy choice.
agent_test: Add an impasse trigger and compare abandonment rate and final score against no trigger.
